Developing a drug takes years, and most candidates never reach patients.

Amortizing the cost of failed drugs across stages, the present value cost of developing a drug is close to $2B. The process takes 13 years on average, with rising clinical trial costs putting further pressure on R&D productivity.

AI could improve those economics by increasing the probability of success and reducing development time, from identifying promising molecules to designing clinical trials and improving patient recruitment.

That may enable companies to pursue therapeutic targets and indications that might otherwise have been uneconomical.

Full piece on why AI will make pharma even bigger: https://t.co/A96FDSSk57

Institutional investors are extremely bullish on the US equity market:

Long non-dealer positioning in US equity futures is up to +$330 billion, its 2nd-highest on record.

This metric covers asset managers, hedge funds, Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), and other institutional investors.

Over the last 6 months, net long positioning in US equity futures has risen by +$100 billion.

This figure is now just $10 billion below its all-time high set in 2024.

By comparison, between 2010 and 2023, institutional positioning never exceeded $150 billion.

Institutional investors are heavily exposed to US equities.

Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak says AI can now carry out cyberattacks in 20 minutes that once took skilled attackers weeks or months.

In his view, companies need to continuously attack their own systems with the latest AI models to stay secure. For startups, that means building automated testing and patching into the development process from the beginning.

Ami joins a16z's Sarah Wang and Zane Lackey to discuss what changed during Black October, why patching is falling behind, the cost of continuous security testing, and why better security architecture matters more than simply buying more tools.

The market for drugs is deep and diversified, and the size of the prize is huge if you get it right. A single blockbuster drug can generate annual revenue on the scale of a major software company.

Pharma has unusual economics – it's a hits business in drug development and an annuity business once a drug succeeds.

AI could change both by improving the odds of success and simultaneously decreasing development time and cost.

The US deficit crisis is accelerating.

BREAKING: Retail investors bought +$730 million in Nvidia, $NVDA, stock on Tuesday, their largest daily purchase since March.

This was preceded by +$590 million on Monday and followed by +$300 million on Wednesday.

In total, retail investors bought +$1.6 billion in Nvidia shares in 3 trading days ending Wednesday, retail's largest 3-day purchase in at least 12 months.

Over the same period, the 2x leveraged long Nvidia ETF, $NVDL, attracted +$401 million in inflows, putting it on track for its largest weekly intake since November 2025.

The 2x leveraged long Nvidia ETF, $NVDU, attracted +$64 million, on track for its largest weekly inflow since February 2026.

Meanwhile, during the first 30 minutes of Thursday’s session, retail investors bought +$455 million of $NVDA stock and sold -$345 million, bringing net purchases to +$111 million, their largest in any first 30 minutes of trading on record.

Retail investors are doubling down on Nvidia.

A complete investigation is necessary.
